transcript.text: What's up, Alex? We do vacation rental
property management. At what point
should I start considering dropping some
of these lower-end properties that don't
necessarily fit the lakefront lifestyle
that I want to build around?
>> This is a process we look at on an
annual basis. Like, do we have
underperforming locations? And is it an
operator issue or is it a market issue?
If we control for the operator, we
think, "No, this is a good operator.
This market is kind of tough for this
particular business." We'll trim the
location, move the operator to a new
location that that we're opening up that
we think is a good market. By dropping
them, what do you gain back? And then,
if you take the resources that you're
going to
put them into something else, at what
point does that return on the something
else outweigh the cost of dropping?
